"**The Dial**" is a song by British band [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)"). It was released on 21 September 2018 through Speedy Wunderground on 7" and streaming services. The song saw the band get "much bolder and louder" than their debut EP, _Lino_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-TG-1) The song is about a loved one suffering from illness. Critics reviewed the song positively.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Squid is a British band made up of Ollie Judge, Louis Borlase, Arthur Leadbetter, Laurie Nankivell and Anton Pearson.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-2) The band would release their debut EP, _Lino_, in 2017 and a debut single, "Terrestrial Changeover Blues (2007–2012)" in 2018.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-TG-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3)

## Music and lyrics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music and lyrics")]

"The Dial" has been described as [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4) The track was produced by [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") and recorded in under 24 hours.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4) According to the band, the song's lyrics revolve around "a dear loved one suffering a horrible illness in hospital".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-LOBF-5) While the patient's blood is being taken, the nurses turn into vampires and suck the blood from the other patients.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3) The track begins with "a tight drum beat and relatively taut, funky guitar strut".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY-6) As the songs continues, the instrumentation grows more intense.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY-6) Judge's vocals "plunge in and out of a forceful, rasping screech" throughout.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Release")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/SXSW_2019_-_Squid_%2847436196911%29.jpg/250px-SXSW_2019_-_Squid_%2847436196911%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SXSW_2019_-_Squid_(47436196911).jpg)

Squid in 2019

"The Dial" was released on 21 September 2018 through Speedy Wunderground.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY2-7) The song was released on streaming services and on a limited edition 7" [vinyl record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonograph_record "Phonograph record").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-LOBF-5) In June 2019, before the release of _[Town Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town\_Centre\_(EP) "Town Centre (EP)")_, Judge called the song a "big, massive step" in their music, and that "everything before ["The Dial"] was more us finding our feet."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY2-7)

On 1 December 2020, as part of an effort to prevent [the Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") from closing, the band put up a signed copy of "The Dial" for auction in order to raise funds.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-8)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")]

Critics responded positively to "The Dial". Reviewing the song for _[The Line of Best Fit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Line\_of\_Best\_Fit "The Line of Best Fit")_, Amelia Maher called it "another electrifying offering" from the band that "shuns predictability in favour of exhilarating energy and excitement".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-LOBF-5) A review of the song for _[DIY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DIY\_(magazine) "DIY (magazine)")_ said the band had "shown themselves to be something really special" and called the track "as funky as it is heavy".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY-6) Gil Green of _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ said the song had a "playful yet anarchist darkness" and an "angular groove that explodes into a spacey crash".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3) In a review for _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash\_(magazine) "Clash (magazine)")_, Robin Murray called the song a "fantastic piece of minimalist guitar music".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4) Jude Rogers of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ said "The Dial" saw Squid "getting much bolder and louder" and that it saw them "siphoning the energy of early 00s groups such as [the Rapture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rapture_(band) "The Rapture (band)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-TG-1)

"**The Dial**" is a song by British band [Squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band) "Squid (band)"). It was released on 21 September 2018 through Speedy Wunderground on 7" and streaming services. The song saw the band get "much bolder and louder" than their debut EP, _Lino_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-TG-1) The song is about a loved one suffering from illness. Critics reviewed the song positively.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Squid is a British band made up of Ollie Judge, Louis Borlase, Arthur Leadbetter, Laurie Nankivell and Anton Pearson.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-2) The band would release their debut EP, _Lino_, in 2017 and a debut single, "Terrestrial Changeover Blues (2007–2012)" in 2018.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-TG-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3)

## Music and lyrics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music and lyrics")]

"The Dial" has been described as [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4) The track was produced by [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") and recorded in under 24 hours.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4) According to the band, the song's lyrics revolve around "a dear loved one suffering a horrible illness in hospital".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-LOBF-5) While the patient's blood is being taken, the nurses turn into vampires and suck the blood from the other patients.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3) The track begins with "a tight drum beat and relatively taut, funky guitar strut".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY-6) As the songs continues, the instrumentation grows more intense.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY-6) Judge's vocals "plunge in and out of a forceful, rasping screech" throughout.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Release")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/SXSW_2019_-_Squid_%2847436196911%29.jpg/250px-SXSW_2019_-_Squid_%2847436196911%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SXSW_2019_-_Squid_(47436196911).jpg)

Squid in 2019

"The Dial" was released on 21 September 2018 through Speedy Wunderground.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY2-7) The song was released on streaming services and on a limited edition 7" [vinyl record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonograph_record "Phonograph record").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-LOBF-5) In June 2019, before the release of _[Town Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town\_Centre\_(EP) "Town Centre (EP)")_, Judge called the song a "big, massive step" in their music, and that "everything before ["The Dial"] was more us finding our feet."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY2-7)

On 1 December 2020, as part of an effort to prevent [the Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") from closing, the band put up a signed copy of "The Dial" for auction in order to raise funds.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-8)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Dial_(song)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reception")]

Critics responded positively to "The Dial". Reviewing the song for _[The Line of Best Fit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Line\_of\_Best\_Fit "The Line of Best Fit")_, Amelia Maher called it "another electrifying offering" from the band that "shuns predictability in favour of exhilarating energy and excitement".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-LOBF-5) A review of the song for _[DIY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DIY\_(magazine) "DIY (magazine)")_ said the band had "shown themselves to be something really special" and called the track "as funky as it is heavy".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-DIY-6) Gil Green of _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ said the song had a "playful yet anarchist darkness" and an "angular groove that explodes into a spacey crash".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-SG-3) In a review for _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash\_(magazine) "Clash (magazine)")_, Robin Murray called the song a "fantastic piece of minimalist guitar music".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-clash-4) Jude Rogers of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ said "The Dial" saw Squid "getting much bolder and louder" and that it saw them "siphoning the energy of early 00s groups such as [the Rapture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rapture_(band) "The Rapture (band)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dial_(song)#cite_note-TG-1)

**Squid** are an English [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band formed in [Brighton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton "Brighton") in 2016.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k1-1) The band consists of Ollie Judge (vocals, drums), Louis Borlase (guitar, vocals), Anton Pearson (guitar, vocals), Laurie Nankivell (bass, brass) and Arthur Leadbetter (keyboards). They are currently based in Bristol.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-NME-5)

A [Windmill scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill_scene "Windmill scene") band,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-6) Squid independently released their debut EP, _LINO_, in 2017, which was followed by several stand-alone singles and the EP _[Town Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town\_Centre\_(EP) "Town Centre (EP)")_ in 2019 on [Speedy Wunderground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground "Speedy Wunderground").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k1-1) Their debut album, _[Bright Green Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright\_Green\_Field "Bright Green Field")_, was released by [Warp Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warp_Records "Warp Records") on 7 May 2021.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k3-7) It received widespread critical acclaim and debuted at No. 4 on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"). Their second album, _[O Monolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O\_Monolith "O Monolith")_, was released in 2023 to similar acclaim. Their third album, _[Cowards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowards\_(album) "Cowards (album)")_, was released in 2025.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Squid_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Squid formed in Brighton, England, in 2016.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-The_Guardian-8) They have cited [Neu!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neu! "Neu!") and [This Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Heat "This Heat") as influences.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-NME-5) In 2019, they released their second EP, titled _Town Centre,_ to critical acclaim.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k1-1)_Town Centre_ was produced by [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") and released on Speedy Wunderground. In March 2020, Squid signed to [Warp Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warp_Records "Warp Records") and have released five singles with them as of April 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-consequenceofsound.net-9) They were planning on touring Europe throughout 2020 before the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k2-10)

Taking advantage of lockdown, the band spent most of 2020 recording what would be their debut album, _[Bright Green Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright\_Green\_Field "Bright Green Field")_, again working with producer Dan Carey. The album was released on 7 May 2021 and was promoted by three singles, "Narrator", "Paddling" and "Pamphlets".

Squid appeared at the [Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival") in June 2022, and appeared at the [Rock en Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_en_Seine "Rock en Seine") and [Paredes de Coura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paredes_de_Coura_Festival "Paredes de Coura Festival") festivals in August 2022. They replaced [Viagra Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viagra_Boys "Viagra Boys") at [La Route Du Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Route_Du_Rock?action=edit&redlink=1 "La Route Du Rock (page does not exist)") festival in August 2023.

Squid recorded their second album, _[O Monolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O\_Monolith "O Monolith")_, in Wiltshire in early 2022, before releasing it on 9 June 2023, once again with Warp Records.

In November 2024, Squid announced their third album, _[Cowards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowards\_(album) "Cowards (album)")_. It was released on 7 February 2025 through Warp Records.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-theskinny-15)

**Squid** are an English [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band formed in [Brighton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton "Brighton") in 2016.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k1-1) The band consists of Ollie Judge (vocals, drums), Louis Borlase (guitar, vocals), Anton Pearson (guitar, vocals), Laurie Nankivell (bass, brass) and Arthur Leadbetter (keyboards). They are currently based in Bristol.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-NME-5)

A [Windmill scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windmill_scene "Windmill scene") band,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-6) Squid independently released their debut EP, _LINO_, in 2017, which was followed by several stand-alone singles and the EP _[Town Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town\_Centre\_(EP) "Town Centre (EP)")_ in 2019 on [Speedy Wunderground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground "Speedy Wunderground").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k1-1) Their debut album, _[Bright Green Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright\_Green\_Field "Bright Green Field")_, was released by [Warp Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warp_Records "Warp Records") on 7 May 2021.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k3-7) It received widespread critical acclaim and debuted at No. 4 on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"). Their second album, _[O Monolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O\_Monolith "O Monolith")_, was released in 2023 to similar acclaim. Their third album, _[Cowards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowards\_(album) "Cowards (album)")_, was released in 2025.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Squid_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Squid formed in Brighton, England, in 2016.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-The_Guardian-8) They have cited [Neu!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neu! "Neu!") and [This Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Heat "This Heat") as influences.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-NME-5) In 2019, they released their second EP, titled _Town Centre,_ to critical acclaim.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k1-1)_Town Centre_ was produced by [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") and released on Speedy Wunderground. In March 2020, Squid signed to [Warp Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warp_Records "Warp Records") and have released five singles with them as of April 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-consequenceofsound.net-9) They were planning on touring Europe throughout 2020 before the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-p4k2-10)

Taking advantage of lockdown, the band spent most of 2020 recording what would be their debut album, _[Bright Green Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright\_Green\_Field "Bright Green Field")_, again working with producer Dan Carey. The album was released on 7 May 2021 and was promoted by three singles, "Narrator", "Paddling" and "Pamphlets".

Squid appeared at the [Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival "Glastonbury Festival") in June 2022, and appeared at the [Rock en Seine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_en_Seine "Rock en Seine") and [Paredes de Coura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paredes_de_Coura_Festival "Paredes de Coura Festival") festivals in August 2022. They replaced [Viagra Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viagra_Boys "Viagra Boys") at [La Route Du Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Route_Du_Rock?action=edit&redlink=1 "La Route Du Rock (page does not exist)") festival in August 2023.

Squid recorded their second album, _[O Monolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O\_Monolith "O Monolith")_, in Wiltshire in early 2022, before releasing it on 9 June 2023, once again with Warp Records.

In November 2024, Squid announced their third album, _[Cowards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowards\_(album) "Cowards (album)")_. It was released on 7 February 2025 through Warp Records.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid_(band)#cite_note-theskinny-15)

**Wide Awake** is a yearly outdoor [music festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_festival "Music festival") held in [Brockwell Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brockwell_Park "Brockwell Park") in London. It was first held in 2021 and its programming largely focuses on [electronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronica "Electronica"), [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop"), and [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"). It has seen headline performances by acts like [Idles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idles "Idles"), [Primal Scream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primal_Scream "Primal Scream"), [King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Gizzard_&_the_Lizard_Wizard "King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard"), [Young Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Fathers "Young Fathers"), and [Kneecap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kneecap_(band) "Kneecap (band)").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wide_Awake_(festival)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

It was first held in [Brockwell Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brockwell_Park "Brockwell Park") in the [London Borough of Lambeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Borough_of_Lambeth "London Borough of Lambeth") on 3 September 2021 and has been held there each year since, although usually at the end of May. Its programming is a collaboration between music bookers Bad Vibrations, Dimensions, LNZRT and Snap Crackle & Pop.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeek-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-Louder21Re-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-Louder22Pre-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-Rolling25Re-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeekInt-5)

The festival was founded by Keith Miller (who runs the music promotion company Bad Vibrations, is head programmer at LNZRT and head of events at several small London venues) and festival director Marcus Weedon. They had previously worked together on the London festival [Field Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_Day_(festival) "Field Day (festival)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-NMEOrigins-6) The first edition of the festival had been planned for 5 June 2020, but was cancelled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeek-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeekInt-5)

**Wide Awake** is a yearly outdoor [music festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_festival "Music festival") held in [Brockwell Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brockwell_Park "Brockwell Park") in London. It was first held in 2021 and its programming largely focuses on [electronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronica "Electronica"), [alternative pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_pop "Alternative pop"), and [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"). It has seen headline performances by acts like [Idles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idles "Idles"), [Primal Scream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primal_Scream "Primal Scream"), [King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Gizzard_&_the_Lizard_Wizard "King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard"), [Young Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Fathers "Young Fathers"), and [Kneecap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kneecap_(band) "Kneecap (band)").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wide_Awake_(festival)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

It was first held in [Brockwell Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brockwell_Park "Brockwell Park") in the [London Borough of Lambeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Borough_of_Lambeth "London Borough of Lambeth") on 3 September 2021 and has been held there each year since, although usually at the end of May. Its programming is a collaboration between music bookers Bad Vibrations, Dimensions, LNZRT and Snap Crackle & Pop.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeek-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-Louder21Re-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-Louder22Pre-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-Rolling25Re-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeekInt-5)

The festival was founded by Keith Miller (who runs the music promotion company Bad Vibrations, is head programmer at LNZRT and head of events at several small London venues) and festival director Marcus Weedon. They had previously worked together on the London festival [Field Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_Day_(festival) "Field Day (festival)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-NMEOrigins-6) The first edition of the festival had been planned for 5 June 2020, but was cancelled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeek-1)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_(festival)#cite_note-MusicWeekInt-5)

Musical artist

**Jojo Orme**, known professionally as **Heartworms**, is an English musician.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-FredPerry-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-:0-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Josephine Orme[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-3) was born in central [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England in 1998 or 1999.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-:0-2) She has Afghan and Pakistani heritage on her father's side, and Danish and Chinese on her mother's.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-4) Orme was raised in [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-dazed1-5) She grew up with the music her mother listened to, including artists such as [Hot Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Chocolate "Hot Chocolate"), [Fleetwood Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleetwood_Mac "Fleetwood Mac"), [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), and [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-rpm-6) She left home at 14 to enter foster care.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-quietus2-7) Orme studied Production and Performance at [South Gloucestershire and Stroud College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Gloucestershire_and_Stroud_College "South Gloucestershire and Stroud College")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme1-8) wanting to become a producer as "there's not many in the industry".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-quietus2-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Orme took the name 'Heartworms' from [the Shins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shins "The Shins") 2017 [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(album) "Heartworms (album)"). She met producer [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") over [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), and he asked her to send him some demos.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-utr1-9) Much of her early career was spent performing at [the Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") venue in Brixton, alongside [Black Country, New Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road "Black Country, New Road"), [Goat Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_Girl "Goat Girl"), [the Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [PVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PVA_(band) "PVA (band)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-11) In 2022, she signed to Carey's [Speedy Wunderground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground "Speedy Wunderground") label, and released the single "Consistent Dedication".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme1-8) Her debut EP _A Comforting Notion_ was released in 2023,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-dazed1-5) alongside a limited edition [Airfix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airfix "Airfix")[Spitfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spitfire "Spitfire") model.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-quietus-12) She went on to earn support slots with [the Kills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kills "The Kills") and [St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Vincent_(musician) "St. Vincent (musician)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme2-13)

In February 2025, Orme's debut album _[Glutton for Punishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glutton\_for\_Punishment\_(album) "Glutton for Punishment (album)")_ was released to critical acclaim, including a five-star review from _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme3-14)

Heartworms' music has been categorised by critics as [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16)[gothic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_rock "Gothic rock")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) and [dance punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_punk "Dance punk").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) She often incorporates elements of [electroclash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroclash "Electroclash"), [post-industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-industrial_music "Post-industrial music"), 1990s and 2000s [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno") and [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)

She said she "discovered [the Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure") and [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees")" while at [university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University "University") and was attracted to what was musically "dark".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-rpm-6) Her other influences include [PJ Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PJ_Harvey "PJ Harvey") and her album _[To Bring You My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Bring\_You\_My\_Love "To Bring You My Love")_ (1995),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-rpm-6)[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Joke "Killing Joke")'s _[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing\_Joke\_(1980\_album) "Killing Joke (1980 album)")_ (1980), [Grauzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauzone "Grauzone")'s _Grauzone_ (1981), [the Sisters of Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sisters_of_Mercy "The Sisters of Mercy")'s _[Floodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floodland\_(album) "Floodland (album)")_ (1987), [Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Cave_and_the_Bad_Seeds "Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds")' _[Push the Sky Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push\_the\_Sky\_Away "Push the Sky Away")_ (2013), [Sóley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%B3ley "Sóley")'s Krómantík (2014), [Nox Arcana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nox_Arcana "Nox Arcana")'s _[Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic\_(Nox\_Arcana\_album) "Gothic (Nox Arcana album)")_ (2015), Drahla's _Useless Coordinates_ (2019),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-17)[Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol_(band) "Interpol (band)") and [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash") - plus classical music composers like [Frédéric Chopin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Chopin "Frédéric Chopin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-18)

Musical artist

**Jojo Orme**, known professionally as **Heartworms**, is an English musician.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-FredPerry-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-:0-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Josephine Orme[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-3) was born in central [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), England in 1998 or 1999.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-:0-2) She has Afghan and Pakistani heritage on her father's side, and Danish and Chinese on her mother's.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-4) Orme was raised in [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham "Cheltenham"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-dazed1-5) She grew up with the music her mother listened to, including artists such as [Hot Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Chocolate "Hot Chocolate"), [Fleetwood Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleetwood_Mac "Fleetwood Mac"), [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), and [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-rpm-6) She left home at 14 to enter foster care.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-quietus2-7) Orme studied Production and Performance at [South Gloucestershire and Stroud College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Gloucestershire_and_Stroud_College "South Gloucestershire and Stroud College")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme1-8) wanting to become a producer as "there's not many in the industry".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-quietus2-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Orme took the name 'Heartworms' from [the Shins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shins "The Shins") 2017 [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(album) "Heartworms (album)"). She met producer [Dan Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Carey_(record_producer) "Dan Carey (record producer)") over [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), and he asked her to send him some demos.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-utr1-9) Much of her early career was spent performing at [the Windmill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Windmill,_Brixton "The Windmill, Brixton") venue in Brixton, alongside [Black Country, New Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Country,_New_Road "Black Country, New Road"), [Goat Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat_Girl "Goat Girl"), [the Last Dinner Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Last_Dinner_Party "The Last Dinner Party") and [PVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PVA_(band) "PVA (band)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-11) In 2022, she signed to Carey's [Speedy Wunderground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speedy_Wunderground "Speedy Wunderground") label, and released the single "Consistent Dedication".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme1-8) Her debut EP _A Comforting Notion_ was released in 2023,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-dazed1-5) alongside a limited edition [Airfix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airfix "Airfix")[Spitfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spitfire "Spitfire") model.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-quietus-12) She went on to earn support slots with [the Kills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kills "The Kills") and [St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Vincent_(musician) "St. Vincent (musician)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme2-13)

In February 2025, Orme's debut album _[Glutton for Punishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glutton\_for\_Punishment\_(album) "Glutton for Punishment (album)")_ was released to critical acclaim, including a five-star review from _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-nme3-14)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Heartworms_(musician)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Artistry")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Heartworms%2C_Green_Door_Store%2C_Brighton%2C_UK_22_March_2023.jpg/250px-Heartworms%2C_Green_Door_Store%2C_Brighton%2C_UK_22_March_2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Heartworms,_Green_Door_Store,_Brighton,_UK_22_March_2023.jpg)

Orme performing at the Green Door Store, Brighton in 2023

Heartworms' music has been categorised by critics as [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16)[gothic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_rock "Gothic rock")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) and [dance punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_punk "Dance punk").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Rigotti,_2025-16) She often incorporates elements of [electroclash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroclash "Electroclash"), [post-industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-industrial_music "Post-industrial music"), 1990s and 2000s [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno") and [electronic dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-Young,_2025-15)

She said she "discovered [the Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure") and [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees")" while at [university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University "University") and was attracted to what was musically "dark".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-rpm-6) Her other influences include [PJ Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PJ_Harvey "PJ Harvey") and her album _[To Bring You My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Bring\_You\_My\_Love "To Bring You My Love")_ (1995),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-rpm-6)[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Joke "Killing Joke")'s _[Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing\_Joke\_(1980\_album) "Killing Joke (1980 album)")_ (1980), [Grauzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauzone "Grauzone")'s _Grauzone_ (1981), [the Sisters of Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sisters_of_Mercy "The Sisters of Mercy")'s _[Floodland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floodland\_(album) "Floodland (album)")_ (1987), [Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Cave_and_the_Bad_Seeds "Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds")' _[Push the Sky Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push\_the\_Sky\_Away "Push the Sky Away")_ (2013), [Sóley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%B3ley "Sóley")'s Krómantík (2014), [Nox Arcana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nox_Arcana "Nox Arcana")'s _[Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic\_(Nox\_Arcana\_album) "Gothic (Nox Arcana album)")_ (2015), Drahla's _Useless Coordinates_ (2019),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-17)[Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol_(band) "Interpol (band)") and [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash") - plus classical music composers like [Frédéric Chopin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Chopin "Frédéric Chopin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartworms_(musician)#cite_note-18)
